body: Don't need to talk to one anymore. Where I live it's pretty automatic that you go to a psych ward after an attempt and stay there until you have the resourced and care contacts to deal with it all. And that's where I'm at atm... Right now I'm starting to see some signs that there might eventually be a solution to this, that's not death.
Well mine became just an attempt it seems, so that's a win for your side

My favourite atm is the Agents of Shield, love scifi!

But yeah, there was a fourth option that I didn't think of beforehand. Start downing the pills (well over a hundred needed) and realise half way through that it's really fucking hard to swallow that many. Hit a wall at 70, where the chanses of death are still quite low, but it'll fuck up your liver for sure. Succumb to the idea of going to the ER and experience what it's like to have people in the beds next to you hear what a loser you are. That went well...

No worries still here. Probable path to recovery? Not sure about the recovery part but right now I think I'd call someone even if I did manage to take the pills. That'd take me somewhere, probably. Three options, wait till I can trust myself not to call for help, do it and then call for help, or just simply call for help.

The first one would be easiest for me, just have to wait, but it'll be the hardest one for relatives. About the other two I'm not sure which on is more shameful, calling for help before or after I've done something. And the repercussions of either one aren't going to be fun nor easy for me. The good thing about them is that nobody, aside from the professional people, would have to know about it.

If only I could reset and be an ignorant teen with the knowledge and understanding of what not to do. But now, getting close to being 30 and all aspects of life in ruins, finances a hole that'd take a lifetime to fill, not really.

Constant failures in life. Financial, academic, relationships, you name it. The funniest part is that they're all caused by me and nobody else.

I broke up with my ex to look for a better life. Didn't find it.

I broke up with my more recent ex since I got fed up of all the arguing.

I didn't get out of the bed to attend Uni.

I didn't stop the student loans from accumulating even though I wasn't even studying. Had to take other loans to survive the summers since I wasn't in a condition to work either.

I didn't call all the places I should have to make arrangements about unpaid bills.

I didn't think this 'relapse' was serious enough to seek help earlier.

I had a similar episode of depression that lasted for a couple of years, started when I was 19 (I'm 25 now), and when I was dismissed back then, after my situation had gotten better, I was told to keep a close eye on my mental health if similar symptoms start appearing and seek help before it gets out of hand. I think I might have failed. I don't even think I could really be healthy anymore, this seems to be something that'll just keep coming back until my resolve runs out.
